test_title: PYST 61: RRB Group D - GA (Held On: 24 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following features is a major design focus for the Zorawar tank?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Amphibious capability and lightweight design**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Zorawar** is an indigenous **Light Tank** developed primarily for the **Indian Army** to operate in difficult terrains where heavy main battle tanks face mobility issues.
 
• A major design focus for the **Zorawar** tank is its **lightweight design**, typically weighing around **25 tonnes**. This allow the tank to be easily transported by air via **C-17 Globemaster** aircraft and deployed rapidly in **high-altitude areas**. ***Hence, the statement regarding lightweight design is correct.***
 
• The tank is equipped with **amphibious capability**, which enables it to navigate across water bodies like rivers and lakes, a critical feature for operations in the **Himalayan region** and riverine terrains. ***Hence, the statement regarding amphibious capability is correct.***
 
• It has been developed collaboratively by the **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** and **Larsen & Toubro (L&T)** to provide the **Indian Army** with a tactical advantage in the **Line of Actual Control (LAC)**.
 
• The **Zorawar** tank is designed to feature high **mobility** and **firepower**, making it suitable for **mountain warfare** where traditional tanks like the **T-90** or **T-72** might struggle due to their weight exceeding **40-50 tonnes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Strategic Necessity:** The project was fast-tracked following the **2020 standoff** with **China** in **Eastern Ladakh**. The **People's Liberation Army (PLA)** had deployed its **Type 15 (ZTQ-15)** light tanks, prompting **India** to develop a similar indigenous capability.
 
• **Naming:** The tank is named after **General Zorawar Singh**, the legendary 19th-century military commander who led successful campaigns in **Ladakh**, **Baltistan**, and **Tibet**.
 
• **Technological Features:** It is expected to integrate **Artificial Intelligence (AI)**, **unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)** integration for better situational awareness, and **Active Protection Systems (APS)** to defend against anti-tank guided missiles.
 
• **Power-to-Weight Ratio:** One of its defining features is a high **power-to-weight ratio**, ensuring it can climb steep gradients and navigate narrow passes in **high-altitude** regions exceeding **15,000 feet**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Project Zorawar:** The **Indian Army** has expressed a requirement for approximately **354** of these light tanks to equip its armored regiments in **mountainous** sectors.
 
• **Trials:** The prototype of the **Zorawar** tank commenced internal trials in **July 2024**, with further **user trials** by the **Army** expected to follow in desert and **high-altitude** environments to test its performance under extreme temperatures.
 
• **Stealth and Detection:** While it incorporates modern electronic warfare suites, it is **not** designed for **naval stealth** or **submarine detection**, as those are naval technologies unrelated to armored land warfare.
 
• **Weaponry:** It is typically armed with a **105mm** main gun capable of firing various types of ammunition and **anti-tank missiles**, providing a balance between lethality and the constraints of a lighter chassis.
</ul
